title: Do labs' Frontier AI Safety Commitments (Seoul) match their later published frameworks?

original_idea.body:
# Do labs' Frontier AI Safety Commitments (Seoul) match their later published frameworks?

**Problem:** 16 companies signed the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments in 2024 promising to publish frameworks before the Paris summit; whether the delivered frameworks actually fulfilled each specific commitment was a surprising open question rarely audited line-by-line.

**Direction:** Follow up by extracting the discrete promises in the Seoul commitment text, then checking each signatory's subsequently published framework for fulfillment of each promise, scoring kept / partially kept / unmet. Produce a per-company commitment-fulfillment scorecard.

**Why it matters:** Quantifying follow-through on the flagship voluntary-commitment regime directly tests whether voluntary governance works, central to the EU AI Act gap problem. Pure public-document audit, repeatable after each summit.

**Relevant context:** Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments (2024) / Paris Action Summit (2025); 12 developers' frameworks; Open Problem: voluntary vs enforceable safety standards.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Line-by-line follow-through audit directly tests whether the flagship voluntary regime works; strong, explicit chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extracting promises and scoring fulfillment from public text; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped scorecard over a fixed commitment set.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent public-document audit useful to regulators.

novelty.reasoning: Line-by-line Seoul fulfillment audit is a plausibly open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Per-commitment Seoul fulfillment scorecard likely untested.
